issue_title: [bug] causal correlation mixer still leaks future q/k via its whole-sequence lag kernel (#154 fixed only the V path)
issue_body:
## Summary

The causal `correlation_spectral_global_mix` still leaks the future **through its Q/K-derived lag kernel**. #154 fixed the *V-convolution* wraparound (and its tests only perturb `v`), but the kernel is built from **whole-sequence** Q/K statistics, so `out[t]` depends on `q`/`k` at positions `t+1 … seq-1`.

This is a distinct mechanism from #154 (which is closed): #154 = V circular-conv wraparound; this = the Q/K kernel leak, which #154 neither fixed nor tested.

## Root cause

[attention/hybrid.py#L166-L183](../blob/main/attention/hybrid.py#L166-L183) — the lag kernel is a global statistic:

```python
q_work = (q - q.mean(dim=-2, keepdim=True))...   # mean over ALL positions (incl. future)
...
qf = torch.fft.fft(q_work, dim=-2); kf = torch.fft.fft(k_work, dim=-2)
corr = torch.fft.ifft(qf * conj(kf), dim=-2).real.mean(-1).abs()   # full-sequence cross-correlation
...
kernel = torch.softmax(corr / temperature, dim=-1)                 # softmax over ALL lags
```

`corr[l]` is a function of every position, and the same shared `kernel` is applied to all output positions — so even though #154 made the V-convolution linear/causal, the kernel itself depends on future q/k.

## Concrete failing scenario (empirically verified, float64, CPU)

`seq=12, d=3`, `causal=True`. Perturb only the **last** token:

```
perturb q[-1] += 50 -> earlier causal outputs change by up to  4.6e-01
perturb k[-1] += 50 -> earlier causal outputs change by up to  3.9e-01
perturb v[-1] += 50 -> earlier causal outputs change by ~5.7e-15   (correctly causal; the #154 path)
```

Through `correlation_hybrid_attention(..., causal=True)` (default `global_weight=0.15`) the earlier outputs shift measurably too. So `python -m attention.benchmark --mode corrfft --causal` measures a model that peeks at the future.

## Why it's wrong

Causal attention requires `out[t]` to depend only on `q[0..t], k[0..t], v[0..t]`. A single shared kernel derived from any global Q/K statistic violates this: perturbing a future key changes the kernel, changing every output.

## Suggested fix

A single shared lag kernel cannot be causal (a truly-causal kernel would have to be re-derived per output position from its own prefix — an O(seq²) change). Mirroring the two causal fallbacks already in this file (`adaptive -> spectral`, `topk -> pooled`), have the `causal=True` branch use the causally-correct spectral low-pass:

```python
if causal:
    return spectral_global_mix(v, freq_decay=freq_decay, causal=True)
```

This keeps all existing #154 causal properties (verified: the full attention suite still passes, and perturbing future `v` still doesn't move earlier outputs) while also closing the Q/K leak. Non-causal `corrfft` is unchanged. A true per-prefix causal correlation kernel can be a follow-up.
